_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: A Babylonian approximation of √2
milestones.detail: The clay tablet YBC 7289 shows a square with its diagonals and gives √2 in base 60 as 1;24,51,10, correct to about six decimal places.

milestones.title: Euclid's Elements
milestones.detail: Euclid organised Greek geometry and number theory into thirteen books of definitions, axioms and proofs — the model of deductive mathematics for two millennia.

milestones.title: Archimedes and the method of exhaustion
milestones.detail: Archimedes found the area of a parabolic segment and showed 3 10/71 < π < 3 1/7 by trapping curves between polygons, anticipating integral calculus.

milestones.title: Rules for zero and negative numbers
milestones.detail: Brahmagupta's Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta treated zero as a number and gave rules for arithmetic with negative quantities.

milestones.title: Al-jabr
milestones.detail: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī's book on calculation by completion and balancing gave systematic methods for linear and quadratic equations; it gave algebra its name.

milestones.title: Cubic and quartic equations solved
milestones.detail: Gerolamo Cardano's Ars Magna published formulas for the roots of cubic and quartic equations, found with Scipione del Ferro, Niccolò Tartaglia and Lodovico Ferrari.

milestones.title: Coordinate geometry
milestones.detail: René Descartes' La Géométrie described curves by equations in coordinates, joining algebra and geometry.

milestones.title: The birth of probability
milestones.detail: Letters between Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat solved the 'problem of points' for dividing the stakes of an unfinished game.

milestones.title: Calculus published
milestones.detail: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz published his differential calculus; Isaac Newton had developed his method of fluxions in the 1660s and set out his mechanics in the Principia (1687).

milestones.title: The law of large numbers
milestones.detail: Jacob Bernoulli's posthumous Ars Conjectandi proved that relative frequencies converge to probabilities.

milestones.title: The bridges of Königsberg
milestones.detail: Leonhard Euler showed that no walk crosses each of the seven bridges of Königsberg exactly once, the first theorem of graph theory.

milestones.title: Euler's Introductio
milestones.detail: Euler's Introductio in analysin infinitorum made the function the central object of analysis and contains the formula $e^{ix} = \cos x + i\sin x$.

milestones.title: Disquisitiones Arithmeticae
milestones.detail: Carl Friedrich Gauss introduced congruence notation and proved the law of quadratic reciprocity, founding modern number theory.

milestones.title: Fourier's theory of heat
milestones.detail: Joseph Fourier's Théorie analytique de la chaleur expanded functions in trigonometric series to solve the heat equation.

milestones.title: Rigour in analysis
milestones.detail: Augustin-Louis Cauchy's Cours d'analyse based calculus on limits and convergence.

milestones.title: Galois theory
milestones.detail: On the eve of his fatal duel, Évariste Galois summarised his theory linking the solvability of polynomial equations to groups of permutations.

milestones.title: Riemann's integral and geometry
milestones.detail: Bernhard Riemann's habilitation work defined the integral now named after him, and his lecture on the foundations of geometry introduced curved spaces of any dimension.

milestones.title: Uncountable infinity
milestones.detail: Georg Cantor proved that the real numbers cannot be listed, so infinite sets come in different sizes.

milestones.title: Analysis Situs
milestones.detail: Henri Poincaré's memoir introduced the fundamental group and homology, founding algebraic topology.

milestones.title: Hilbert's problems
milestones.detail: David Hilbert's address to the International Congress of Mathematicians in Paris posed open problems — ten in the lecture itself, 23 in the published text — that shaped twentieth-century research.

milestones.title: The Lebesgue integral
milestones.detail: Henri Lebesgue's thesis Intégrale, longueur, aire built measure theory and a more powerful integral.

milestones.title: Incompleteness
milestones.detail: Kurt Gödel proved that any consistent formal system containing arithmetic has true statements it cannot prove.

milestones.title: Axioms for probability
milestones.detail: Andrey Kolmogorov's Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung founded probability on measure theory.

milestones.title: Computable numbers
milestones.detail: Alan Turing defined computation with abstract machines and showed that some problems cannot be decided by any algorithm.

milestones.title: The simplex method
milestones.detail: George Dantzig's simplex algorithm made linear programming practical for planning and optimisation.

milestones.title: The fast Fourier transform
milestones.detail: James Cooley and John Tukey published the FFT, computing discrete Fourier transforms in O(n log n) operations.

milestones.title: The four colour theorem
milestones.detail: Kenneth Appel and Wolfgang Haken proved that the regions of every planar map can be coloured with four colours so that neighbouring regions always differ, with substantial help from a computer.

milestones.title: Public-key cryptography
milestones.detail: Following Diffie and Hellman's key exchange (1976), Rivest, Shamir and Adleman published the RSA cryptosystem based on the difficulty of factoring.

milestones.title: Fermat's Last Theorem
milestones.detail: Andrew Wiles's proof, completed with Richard Taylor, showed that xⁿ + yⁿ = zⁿ has no positive integer solutions for n > 2.

milestones.title: The Poincaré conjecture
milestones.detail: Grigori Perelman completed the proof that every simply connected closed 3-manifold is a 3-sphere, building on Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow.
